newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan buys second jet cargo amid refinery problem.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan buys second jet cargo amid refinery problem.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has bought by tender a second cargo of jet fuel to compensate for shortages during the partial shutdown of the Taoyuan refinery, a CPC source said on Thursday.
The 32,000-tonne cargo of jet fuel, for October 1-31 delivery, was awarded at $247.82 per tonne to a U.S. major, the seller confirmed.
On Wednesday, a separate cargo was awarded to a German trader at $244.80 per tonne on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung or Shen Ao.
The cargo was awarded on a fixed price and not on a floating price basis had ben earlier expected.
Traders said CPC bought the second cargo due to the unexpected shutdown of a 120,000-barrel-per-day crude distillation unit at the Taoyuan refinery earlier this week.
CPC had earlier cancelled a tender to buy jet fuel for October delivery due to high offers ranging between just under $250 to over $260 per tonne, c-and-f basis.
On Thursday CPC said it aimed to reopen one of two offloading units at the port that feeds the refinery.
The offloading units were closed last weekend owing to unspecified pipeline problems.
The Taoyuan refinery produces 60,000 tonnes of jet fuel a month at full capacity.
